_README: Pinned SHA-256 digests for the files GET /api/waf/:filename is allowed to replay.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. /api/waf/ serves third-party JavaScript from OUR origin, at
runtime, on every legacy-bank preset load. That is same-origin code execution in the
operator's browser on a box whose WebSocket exposes system_update — and a
`script-src 'self'` CSP cannot see it, because /api/waf/ IS 'self'. Audit L10 F-109.
The proxy is fail-closed: with this table empty, GMBOOP_WAF_PROXY=pinned (the
default) refuses every file, without making any outbound request. The built-in
sf2:default bank and every imported SF2 bank are unaffected — they never go through
this route. Only the opt-in legacy WAF CDN banks do.
HOW TO FILL IT IN. Do NOT paste the digest of whatever the CDN served during a
build: that pins the attack, not the artefact. Fetch each file over a channel whose
provenance you have checked, then:
curl -fsSL https://surikov.github.io/webaudiofontdata/sound/<name>.js -o /tmp/<name>.js
sha256sum /tmp/<name>.js
and add "<name>.js": "<64 hex chars>" below, in a commit that says where the bytes
came from. Keys starting with an underscore are documentation and are ignored.
The file set is large (128 melodic entries per bank suffix, plus 47 drum notes per
kit), so pin the banks you actually ship rather than all of them.
ESCAPE HATCH. GMBOOP_WAF_PROXY=open restores the pre-audit behaviour (replay
anything the CDN returns, no integrity check) and logs a warning at startup.
GMBOOP_WAF_PROXY=off disables the route entirely.
